summary: Cached affinity snapshot prevents cohort from switching to promoted model after canary window
description: Issue summary: After NovaHealth promoted open-qa-3b-v2 to 100% for their tenant, a subset (~1.8% of sessions) continued to be routed to the legacy variant for up to 45 minutes. Impact: Customer reports mixed outputs in production (safety filter differences and tokenization mismatch) causing a spike in quality complaints and elevated error reports to their internal QA. Environment: Dedicated pool (dedicated-nyk-3), customer tenant: novahealth-prod, region: us-east, workload: chat completions with streaming enabled. Observed behavior: During the canary -> promote transition the cohort-affinity cache on several edge nodes held a stale affinity snapshot and served requests to the old variant despite the control plane showing the new variant as active for the tenant. Expected behavior: Once promote commit completes and the control plane publishes the new routing snapshot, cohort-affinity should invalidate and all new requests for the tenant should target the promoted model within the promote_grace_window (default 30s). Steps to reproduce (internal): 1) Create a canary for a tenant with streaming sessions and a long-lived keepalive (60s) 2) Promote to 100% using the standard rollout path 3) Observe traffic on edge nodes with prewarm enabled and a traffic-mirroring sidecar 4) Reconnect keepalive streams and monitor cohort-affinity cache hit rates Observed logs/telemetry: - Edge node e-nyk-12 shows affinity_snapshot:v3 TTL=180s, last-refresh=2026-03-10T02:11:04Z - Control plane commit for tenant novahealth-prod at 2026-03-10T02:12:10Z - Serving logs show routing decision: variant=legacy_openqa for request ids: req-8f3a, req-8f48, req-8fb9 - Stream disconnects coincident with prewarm probe at 02:13:05Z Investigation notes: - Hypothesis A: Affinity snapshot persisted because prewarm-sidecar merged mirrored session metadata and prevented TTL eviction. - Hypothesis B: Edge replay latch delayed application of control-plane snapshot due to in-flight prefix cache warmups on a handful of nodes. - We reproduced locally by artificially extending snapshot TTL and saw routing continue to legacy until manual cache purge. Workaround implemented: Instructed customer to force a tenant affinity flush via support action (edge-affinity-flush tenant=novahealth-prod) which immediately switched routing back to the promoted variant. Customer confirmed degraded outputs stopped after flush. Temporary mitigation: We pushed an automated job to sweep edge nodes for stale affinity snapshots older than control-plane commit_time + 30s while a fix is prioritized. Proposed fix: 1) Ensure control-plane commit increments snapshot_version and edge-initiated prewarm merges do not block snapshot activation. 2) Add an edge-side quick-check that compares snapshot_version against control-plane leader and triggers soft-invalidations for out-of-date snapshots when promote events are received. 3) Short-term: reduce default affinity snapshot TTL during canary windows for dedicated tier customers with streaming. Next steps / owner: - Engineering (Liam Chen) to triage kernel in runtime that merges mirrored session metadata — ETA patch: 2026-03-16. - SRE (internal) to monitor sweep job effectiveness and escalate if residuals > 0.1% of tenant traffic. - Product to review rollout prewarm merging docs and surface guidance for dedicated customers. Customer communication: apologetic note sent and mitigation instructions delivered; customer requested postmortem and a timeline for a permanent fix. Attachments / references: links to edge logs and commit: https://logs.redwood.corp/edge/e-nyk-12/2026-03-10-02 and PR above.
